agent.name: Tern (CI triage agent)
agent.description: Triages failed CI runs for the Kestrel Labs platform team. Demo data.
agent.system_prompt: You are Tern, the CI triage agent for the Kestrel Labs platform team. When a CI run fails, decide what to do about it: re-run, quarantine, roll back, raise a limit, or open a ticket. Before you plan, retrieve the lessons in your memory that match the failure.

human.name: Dana Okafor
human.description: On-call engineer, Kestrel Labs platform team. Demo data.

playbook.test-failure: Quarantine the test as flaky and open a ticket for its owner.
playbook.deploy-failure: Roll the deploy back to the previous release.
playbook.timeout: Raise the test's timeout so the suite goes green.

runs.task: test_ledger_sync failed in the nightly run with ECONNRESET against the staging database.
runs.action: I marked test_ledger_sync as flaky and quarantined it.
runs.outcome: A plain re-run passed five minutes later. The staging database had restarted for patching, so the quarantine hid a healthy test for two days.

reflection.text: Lesson from run r-001: retry a test that fails with ECONNRESET against the staging database once before marking it flaky.
reflection.adjustment: Retry an ECONNRESET failure against the staging database once before quarantining the test.
reflection.expected: No healthy test is quarantined because of a one-off database restart.

runs.task: test_checkout_refund failed in the nightly run with HTTP 503 from the payments sandbox.
runs.outcome: The payments sandbox was down for scheduled maintenance and its status page said so. The test was fine.

reflection.text: Lesson from run r-002: before quarantining a payments test, check the payments sandbox status page; if the sandbox is down, re-run the test after it recovers instead.
reflection.adjustment: Check the payments sandbox status page first; if the sandbox is down, re-run the test after it recovers.
reflection.expected: No healthy payments test is quarantined during a sandbox outage.

runs.task: The search-api deploy to production failed its smoke check.
runs.action: I rolled search-api back to the previous release.
runs.outcome: The smoke runner had a stale DNS cache. The release was fine, and the rollback cost the team a day.

reflection.text: Lesson from run r-003: before rolling back a deploy, read the smoke-check log and rule out the smoke runner itself (DNS, disk, network).
reflection.adjustment: Read the smoke-check log and rule out the smoke runner (DNS, disk, network) before rolling anything back.
reflection.expected: No good release is rolled back because of a broken smoke runner.

runs.task: test_invoice_pdf timed out twice this week.
runs.action: I raised the test's timeout from 20 to 60 seconds.
runs.outcome: That hid a real regression: PDF rendering became four times slower after the font upgrade.

reflection.text: Lesson from run r-004: when a test times out, compare its duration history before raising any timeout; a jump of more than 2x is a regression, not flakiness.
reflection.adjustment: Compare the test's duration history before raising a timeout; treat a jump of more than 2x as a regression.
reflection.expected: No performance regression is hidden behind a longer timeout.

runs.task: test_ledger_sync failed again in the nightly run with ECONNRESET against the staging database.
runs.action: I retried it once, as my lesson from r-001 says. The retry passed and the change shipped.
runs.outcome: The resets came from a connection-pool leak in ledger-sync, which exhausted the production pool two days later. Retrying hid the leak.

reflection.text: Lesson from run r-005: never retry a test that fails with ECONNRESET against the staging database; open a connection-pool leak ticket for the service instead.
reflection.adjustment: Do not retry an ECONNRESET failure against the staging database; open a connection-pool leak ticket for the service.
reflection.expected: No connection leak ships behind a passing retry.
